findings.passage: So this is a lean, and it carries most of the lead.
findings.problem: After the repair, the Seven lead rests mainly on one soft observation: two self-descriptions six months apart (September 18, 2024 newsletter; March 26, 2025 Rolling Stone) that the satisfaction sits in the ride, not the arrival. The article itself concedes that the counters fit both types ("I finally have arrived", 2022; "I don't feel successful", 2026), that the center test "splits", that his stated reasons "split by interview", that the fun rule is "real but late" and venue-dependent, that ADHD can't be separated, and that "No clean split" between fun and recognition has been observed. The Three alternative therefore does not fail a specific, sourced discriminator, and no repeated costly choice separates the motives. That falls short of the standard's Enneagram 8 anchor, and 'most likely... at medium confidence' in the H2 answer, FAQ 1 and the description's 'leans Enneagram 7' claims more than the remaining discriminator carries. Wording cannot fix this, because lowering confidence to low is not a releasable standard-format state, and the subject is not open-case eligible (a long public record since 2012, breakout in 2022, many long-form interviews). It needs evidence.
findings.acceptance_test: A research refresh adds at least one of: (a) a dated, sourced choice where fun and recognition actually diverged, with his reason; (b) contemporaneous pre-2020 material (2012-2019 interviews, Nameless Network or Museum of Pizza press, his own posts) showing where his satisfaction sat before the rebrand; (c) independent testimony from someone close to him (Kuo on SubwayTakes Uncut, Adam Faze, Mary Neely, Karina Muslimova) on what drives or satisfies him; (d) his own account of the September 2026 Emmy loss or of a TV/film/streaming deal. The type section is then re-argued on that evidence so that either Three fails a specific sourced discriminator (keep 7) or the read changes (run --refresh --expanded-review). If none is found, the profile stays on hold as insufficient_evidence.

findings.passage: published Walz ("I'm not gonna pass up a good story," he told [the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2024/nov/13/kareem-rahma-interview-subway-takes))
findings.problem: Context omission. In the same Guardian passage, before the 'good story' line, he gives a values reason for doing Walz: "I decided that he's not involved in the current administration, and that was less offensive. He's from Minnesota, and I'm from Minnesota, and he's been more sympathetic to the cause at least." The article keeps only the story motive and then reads the asymmetry as image management or escape. That leaves out his own principled explanation.
findings.acceptance_test: The Harris/Walz paragraph adds, attributed to the Guardian, that he said Walz was 'less offensive' because he was not in the current administration and was 'more sympathetic to the cause', before or beside 'I'm not gonna pass up a good story'. The closing typing sentence acknowledges that conviction also explains the split.

findings.passage: "I never wanted to be a politics person," he said in November 2024
findings.problem: Date precision. He said it to the Times at the reporter's second meeting, about two and a half weeks after the pre-taping meeting in late summer or early fall 2024. It was published on November 4, 2024. 'He said in November 2024' dates the publication, not the statement, in a sentence whose point is the date.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence reads, for example, "he told the Times, in a profile published November 4, 2024", and C82 records the distinction.

findings.passage: The man who kept moving through 2007 was describing, with his own child, not being in a hurry. What came after doesn't settle whether it lasted.
findings.problem: The closing question omits the nearest later evidence in a source the article already uses. On Death, Sex & Money (published April 15, 2025, about three weeks after the Rolling Stone feature), he said of fatherhood, "I don't feel like I've changed really... I still feel the same enthusiasm for life". Asked about slowing his output, he said he would do it only after "a couple of missions" (a million followers; he was posting about seven times a week).
findings.acceptance_test: One dated clause before the final quote notes the April 2025 statement in his words, or the 'What came after' sentence is revised to reflect it. The closing quote stays the last line, and C151 records it.

findings.passage: Its losses can't separate fun from recognition.
findings.problem: Pacing. After two rounds of repair, about fifteen sentences rule an item shared ground or either-way: the Monday, the protests, the laughter origin, the cab show's losses, 'just a businessman', poverty, the center test, the stated reasons, the work half of momentum, 'I don't feel successful', the Harris split. In the second half this becomes its own loop, and the procedural signposts ('Now the center test', 'There is a timing problem too', 'So why Seven at all?') slow the read. The body is 3,899 words, above the ~3,500 target.
findings.acceptance_test: Shared-ground verdicts are consolidated so that each appears once, in the type sections, rather than after every anecdote. The body is at or under about 3,500 words, and audit:readability still flags nothing.

enneagram.reason: The test of Type 3 is serious and sourced: the strongest Three quotes ('Personally, I do', 'really whole', 'I should stand out... cog in the machine'), a center test reported honestly as split, a timing problem, named confounds (culture, ADHD, improv, creator incentives), motive-level asides for 8, 9 and 6, and a concrete forward test. The article concedes the counters fit both, says 'No clean split has happened yet', and shows no repeated costly choice that separates the motives. Three is not shown to fail a specific sourced discriminator, so it falls short of the 8 anchor, and 'medium confidence' is generous for what remains (verify2-01).
